doc.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023

title: Father's advice on ego, Zoom and closing
summary: His father warned against ego; they close, and he mentions subbing in Rat Pack shows.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Yeah. And my father always made sure that I didn’t let ego get in my way. My father was — “We don’t do any ego crap.” You know? “If you play good that’s great. That’s what you need to do. Don’t — you don’t need to tell people how good you play. If you play good they’ll hear it. So don’t get that ego trip going.” So I never did.
You know that’s a very quotable, Tom, so that’s the best way I can think to end this session, and I very much appreciate your time and you’ve been a joy to talk to.

Well likewise. It’s good to see what you look like, and I guess you see what I look like too. I was really concerned that this whole thing wasn’t going to happen because you know I do everything on the computer, I do banking and do all this stuff. But I did one Zoom thing for that “Trumpet Players over 50” — oh what a disaster. “Can you hear me?” “No I can’t hear you.” “Wait fix that.” Luckily I had Danny Falcone here next to me, no hit this button, do that. This was like a piece of cake. This was nice.
Well I hope I get to meet you in person sometime.
I hope so. I think I should come out to Las Vegas.

Yeah well we don’t have a hell of a lot going on for horn players now. There’s plenty of work for trios and a saxophone player right now. There are very few things using a horn. I sub right now at the Rat Pack shows, about Sammy, Frank, and Dean, and that’s got like two trumpets, a trombone and a sax. Four horns. And that gets a good little blow for you, you know. It gets me out of the practice room. I get tired of listening to myself. Like you’ve got to play with a band once in a while. It’s like a sport, you can’t just practice you’ve got to play the game.
Well said. All right. Thanks a lot.
